summary: ASTRA Health is a space health intelligence platform that integrates real biomedical data from the SpaceX Inspiration4 mission, published by NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), with space weather information from NASA DONKI. Its goal is to identify physiological shifts that may go unnoticed when results are evaluated solely against broad, general clinical ranges. To achieve this, it establishes an individualized personal baseline, analyzes multiple organ systems, and provides a full-body digital twin, experimental risk indicators, explainable alerts, and a pre- and post-mission timeline. It also incorporates ASTRA Vision, an experimental computer vision module designed to estimate fatigue, drowsiness, and distraction cues, alongside wellbeing tracking tools, mission scenario simulations, and offline functionality. ASTRA aims to support astronaut health surveillance and, in the future, contribute to the occupational safety of workers in extreme Earth environments.
details:
WHAT PROBLEM DOES IT ADDRESS?

During spaceflights, the human body experiences concurrent systemic changes across multiple physiological systems. However, physiological data is traditionally analyzed in isolated silos and compared against general, population-wide laboratory reference ranges. This approach can mask meaningful changes for an individual, especially when biometric values remain technically within conventional clinical thresholds.

ASTRA investigates this challenge using public data from the four civilian crew members of the Inspiration4 mission. In the team’s analysis, comparing post-flight measurements against each individual's baseline revealed shared systemic patterns: C-reactive protein (CRP) increased by an average of 47.6%, glucose increased by 24.1%, total white blood cells decreased by 14.5%, and absolute neutrophils decreased by 13.4% at R+1. Notably, only 1 out of 79 complete blood count (CBC) values fell outside the standard clinical range specified in the dataset. These findings are exploratory and derived from a small sample size of four individuals; they do not establish direct causality nor can they be broadly generalized to all space travelers.

WHAT DID WE DEVELOP AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

ASTRA Health is an integrated system built upon three primary components:

  1. ASTRA Monitor: Integrates biomedical data, benchmarks every marker against personal baselines, and visualizes deviations, trends, and targeted alerts.
  2. ASTRA Twin: Delivers an anatomical full-body digital twin featuring multi-system color-coded status mapping (traffic-light indicators), a full mission timeline, and longitudinal comparative tools.
  3. ASTRA Intelligence: Computes an experimental Health Risk Score from 0 to 100, detects multi-system anomalies, and generates contextual explanations and actionable recommendations tied directly to cited NASA data sources.

The platform also includes:

  • ASTRA Vision: Analyzes facial indicators via camera feed to estimate fatigue, drowsiness, stress, and distraction. It utilizes the MediaPipe Face Landmarker paired with a YOLO11s model served through FastAPI. All facial processing is performed entirely on-device; video frames are never transmitted or stored.
  • Wellbeing & Sleep: Tracks daily sleep metrics, mood, subjective stress, operational workload, and symptoms; supports wearable telemetry ingestion via CSV.
  • Physiology & Radiation: Correlates NASA DONKI solar events with radiation exposure models and NASA technical literature. Synthetic vital signs are explicitly disclosed as synthetic.
  • Scenario Simulator: Enables exploration of prolonged mission durations, cumulative sleep loss, and solar storm events. Simulated projections are strictly demarcated from empirical measurements.
  • Add Crew Member: Facilitates the onboarding of new profiles and custom lab panels via form input or CSV upload.
  • Offline-First Architecture: A dedicated Windows desktop application powered by local SQLite storage with automated background synchronization once internet connectivity is restored.

Every data point is explicitly tagged as REAL, DERIVED, or SIMULATED/SYNTHETIC. The system presents its scientific data sources transparently and clearly communicates that all scores and alerts are experimental indicators, not clinical medical diagnoses.

WHAT ARE THE EXPECTED BENEFITS AND IMPACT?

ASTRA aims to assist mission flight surgeons and biomedical teams in identifying which organ systems require monitoring, understanding which physiological perturbations persist over time, and reviewing the empirical evidence backing each alert. Moving beyond static population ranges to an individualized baseline enables an integrated, holistic perspective on crew health.

Its design principles also extend directly to extreme environments on Earth. In a future adaptation, ASTRA could support fatigue and wellbeing surveillance for heavy mining machinery operators, long-haul transport drivers, aviators, and personnel working extended shifts in remote or isolated sites. In regions such as Ayacucho, Peru, for instance, this technology could be explored to bolster occupational safety in high-altitude mining operations. This terrestrial application represents a prospective expansion roadmap, not a finalized industrial or clinical validation.

WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, AND SOFTWARE DID WE USE?

  • Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS 4.
  • Runtime / Development Environment: Bun.
  • Backend & API: Python, FastAPI, and Uvicorn.
  • Data Processing & Analytics: Python, pandas, requests, and Jupyter Notebooks.
  • Computer Vision: MediaPipe Face Landmarker, Ultralytics YOLO11s, and PyTorch.
  • Visualization: Custom native SVG visualizations; data analysis prototype using Streamlit and Plotly.
  • Desktop Application: Electron, electron-builder, and SQLite.
  • Data Formats: CSV datasets and structured JSON schemas for data ingestion and pipeline exports.
  • Scientific & Environmental Data Sources: NASA OSDR, NASA DONKI, NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), and NASA EPIC.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE OR INNOVATIVE?

The innovation lies in unifying human spaceflight biomedical records, space environmental telemetry, and real-time computer vision fatigue detection into a single coherent platform. Instead of presenting fragmented data tables, ASTRA constructs a personalized physiological baseline, integrates diverse organ systems into a digital twin, and maps multi-system progression across the entire mission lifecycle. Furthermore, it enforces strict transparency by distinguishing real, derived, and simulated values, and features an offline-first desktop architecture for disconnected operations. The platform is architected to scale from individual astronauts to extreme terrestrial workforces.

WHAT LIMITATIONS AND FACTORS DID WE CONSIDER?

  • The primary human dataset is based on the four civilian participants of the Inspiration4 mission; observations are exploratory and cannot be generalized across larger populations.
  • There was no terrestrial control group within the primary dataset analyzed, meaning observed changes cannot be attributed solely to a single environmental stressor.
  • Inspiration4 lacks publicly released in-flight sleep, continuous fatigue, or heart-rate telemetry; any vital sign series or operational stress scenarios representing these variables are explicitly tagged as synthetic or simulated.
  • OSD-681 represents an animal microgravity analog (hindlimb unloading/head-down tilt), not human physiology.
  • Curiosity RAD provides surface radiation data from Mars and is referenced strictly for environmental context, not as direct dosimetry for Inspiration4.
  • The YOLO11s model was trained on driver drowsiness datasets, not astronaut cohorts; its implementation within ASTRA Vision is experimental and has not been clinically validated.
  • The Health Risk Score is an experimental metric, not a clinical probability or diagnostic evaluation.
  • The system is designed as an investigative decision-support and surveillance tool, never as a replacement for certified medical professionals.
